source_coverage: All seven bullet points of the class notes (Unit 3) are covered; nothing on photosynthesis or uncouplers.

concepts.name: Cellular respiration (overall)
concepts.summary: Cells break down glucose with oxygen to make ATP, releasing CO2 and water.
facts: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + ATP
Aerobic respiration yields roughly 30–38 ATP per glucose in total

misconceptions.wrong: Cells 'breathe' oxygen directly to make energy, so oxygen is used in every stage
misconceptions.why_wrong: Only the last step (the electron transport chain) uses O2; glycolysis needs no oxygen

concepts.name: Glycolysis
concepts.summary: In the cytoplasm, one glucose is split into 2 pyruvate, netting 2 ATP and 2 NADH, with no oxygen needed.
facts: Happens in the cytoplasm
glucose → 2 pyruvate
Net 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose
Does not require oxygen

misconceptions.wrong: Glycolysis stops when oxygen runs out
misconceptions.why_wrong: Glycolysis is anaerobic; it keeps going as long as NAD+ is regenerated (e.g. by fermentation)

concepts.name: Pyruvate oxidation and the Krebs cycle
concepts.summary: In the mitochondrial matrix, pyruvate is fully oxidized to CO2, loading electrons onto NADH and FADH2 and making 2 ATP.
facts: Takes place in the mitochondrial matrix
Releases CO2
Produces NADH, FADH2 and 2 ATP per glucose

misconceptions.wrong: The Krebs cycle makes most of the cell's ATP
misconceptions.why_wrong: It makes only 2 ATP directly; its main job is loading NADH/FADH2 for the electron transport chain

concepts.name: Electron transport chain
concepts.summary: On the inner mitochondrial membrane, NADH and FADH2 hand electrons down a chain of proteins; oxygen is the final electron acceptor and becomes water.
facts: Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane
NADH and FADH2 donate electrons
O2 is the final electron acceptor and is reduced to water
Cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) is the last complex, which hands electrons to O2

misconceptions.wrong: If cells stop using oxygen, it must be because there is no oxygen around
misconceptions.why_wrong: Oxygen is only used when electrons reach complex IV; if the chain is blocked, oxygen sits unused even when plentiful

concepts.name: Chemiosmosis and ATP synthase
concepts.summary: The ETC pumps protons to build a gradient; protons flowing back through ATP synthase make about 26–34 ATP per glucose.
facts: Proton gradient across the inner membrane drives ATP synthase
Produces ~26–34 ATP per glucose — most of the cell's ATP

misconceptions.wrong: ATP synthase can keep making ATP even if the electron transport chain stops
misconceptions.why_wrong: Without electron flow there is no proton pumping, so the gradient collapses and ATP synthase stalls

concepts.name: Fermentation
concepts.summary: Without a working ETC, cells regenerate NAD+ by turning pyruvate into lactate (muscle) or ethanol + CO2 (yeast), getting only 2 ATP per glucose.
facts: Regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can continue
Muscle cells make lactic acid (lactate); yeast make alcohol and CO2
Only 2 ATP per glucose
Each glucose fermented in muscle gives 2 lactate

misconceptions.wrong: Fermentation makes extra energy as a backup
misconceptions.why_wrong: It makes no ATP itself; it only recycles NAD+ so glycolysis's 2 ATP can continue

concepts.name: Electron transport chain poisons
concepts.summary: Chemicals like cyanide block cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), so the ETC stops and ATP production collapses within minutes.
facts: Cyanide blocks cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV)
Blocking complex IV stops the whole chain and oxygen use
ATP production collapses within minutes

misconceptions.wrong: Cyanide-type poisons work by stopping oxygen from reaching the cell
misconceptions.why_wrong: Oxygen still arrives; the cell simply can't use it because complex IV is blocked

concepts.name: Enzymes, temperature and pH
concepts.summary: Enzymes lower activation energy; their activity depends on temperature and pH.
facts: Enzymes lower activation energy
Activity is affected by temperature and pH
Cooling slows enzymes; high heat can denature them

misconceptions.why_wrong: Mild cooling only slows enzymes reversibly; denaturation is caused by high heat or extreme pH
